_comment: North Port–Bradenton–Sarasota, FL MSA — Manatee and Sarasota counties. Ingested from the ChatGPT Work research workbook 2026-08-03. NOT YET IMPORTED as of ingest; the owner APPROVED the projected split on 2026-08-03 and it is now recorded in `expected_publish` below, so every subsequent project/publish run re-asserts it.
_envelope_comment: Derived from the MSA COUNTY LIST, not the observed venue bbox (Toledo precedent). Union of the OSM boundary bboxes for Manatee (relation/1210690, lat 27.2080..27.6467, lng -82.8230..-82.0543) and Sarasota (relation/1210734, lat 26.9454..27.3898, lng -82.7054..-82.0567), rounded OUTWARD to 0.01 deg. WATER CHECK: lngMin -82.83 is Gulf water off Anna Maria Island and admits only sea. KNOWN SOFT EDGE, recorded rather than tightened: latMax 27.65 is Manatee's genuine northern county line, which is also the Hillsborough County line, so the envelope's top edge abuts the Tampa–St. Petersburg MSA. That is the true MSA boundary and tightening below it would violate the county-list rule; the `states` filter does not help here because Tampa is also FL. If a Tampa-metro row is ever admitted, tighten deliberately and record the row that forced it, exactly as toledo.json did for Cedar Point. Cross-check: contains all 24 workbook venues.
_geocode_comment: 2 of the 24 venues produce no coordinate from any query rung, INVESTIGATED before the flag was set. BOTH carry no street address at all in the workbook (venice-northeast-venice-park, manatee-john-marble), so they only ever reach the name-based rungs and Nominatim does not hold those names as POIs — the honest fix is an address, not a retry. Every miss is a genuine HTTP 200 with an empty result set, not rate limiting: scripts/lib/geocode-nominatim.mjs throws on any non-200, so an empty result cannot be a masked failure. Set to false so these 2 import as gate-blocked drafts in the work queue instead of aborting the metro; the publish gate holds each on 'no coordinate'. THIS COUNT WAS 4 UNTIL 2026-08-05, and the two that recovered were exactly the two this note had called a probable workbook address error — they were neither. sarasota-laurel-park (509 Collins Road) and commercial-dill-dinkers-sarasota (500 Tallevast Road) both resolve high against the current ladder. Do not read a geocode miss as evidence that an address is wrong; it is evidence about the ladder on the day it ran.
_expected_publish_comment: The projected split as APPROVED BY THE OWNER on 2026-08-05, recorded so --stage=project and --stage=publish both re-assert it and fail the run on any divergence. If a later run disagrees with this block, fix the pipeline or the data — never edit this block to match the output. SUPERSEDES the 2026-08-03 block (count 17). The +5 splits evenly across the two causes: THREE rows moved on ADR-16 alone (highland-ridge-park, mckibben-park, c-v-walton-racquet-center — all held on 'coordinate precision low'), and TWO moved on the re-geocode alone (laurel-park and dill-dinkers, both held on 'no coordinate'). lakewood-ranch-park was ALREADY publishing and stays: its OSM anchor is named 'Lakewood Ranch Community Park' while the workbook and Manatee County both say 'Lakewood Ranch Park', which was hand-checked on 2026-08-05 against mymanatee.org — same 5350 Lakewood Ranch Blvd, six courts. Its 2471 m township-guard distance is measured against ONE segment of a multi-segment boulevard whose other segment lies 1.75 km the far side, with the park between them; the distance is a road-geometry artifact, not a mislocation.
